question.text:
Which of the following set of vectors are linearly dependent ?

  1. $\left\{ \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}, \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} \right\}$
     
  2. $\left\{ \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 4 \\ 6 \end{bmatrix}, \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix} \right\}$
     
  3. $\left\{ \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}, \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix} \right\}$
     
  4. $\left\{ \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}, \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 4 \\ 6 \end{bmatrix},\begin{bmatrix} 6 \\ 3 \\ 11 \end{bmatrix} , \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 3 \\ -4 \end{bmatrix} \right\}$
question.subject: Linear Algebra

question.text:
Let $A$ and $B$ be invertible square matrices of order $n$, and let $k$ be a non-zero scalar. Which of the following statements is not always true ?

  1. $\det(AB^{-1}A^T)=\dfrac{(\det A)^2}{\det B}$
     
  2. $\det(\operatorname{adj}(A))=(\det A)^{n-1}$
     
  3. $\det(A+kI)=\det(A)+k^n$
     
  4. $\det(A^{-1}B^T)=\dfrac{\det B}{\det A}$
question.subject: Linear Algebra

question.text:
If product of matrix $A=\begin{bmatrix}\cos^{2}\theta &\cos \theta \sin \theta \\  \cos \theta \sin \theta &\sin ^{2} \theta \end{bmatrix}$ and $B=\begin{bmatrix}\cos^{2}\phi &\cos \phi \sin \phi \\  \cos \phi \sin \phi &\sin ^{2} \phi \end{bmatrix}$ is a null matrix, then $\theta$ and $\phi$ differ by an

  1. odd multiple of $\pi$
     
  2. even multiple of $\pi$
     
  3. odd multiple of $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$
     
  4. even multiple of $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$
question.subject: Linear Algebra
